 Prayer :

Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of the
 Motor Vehicles Act, seeking to set aside the judgment and decree da
 12.09.2022 passed in M.C.O.P. No.306 of 2012, by the Exclusive Moto
 Accident Claims Tribunal, Presiding Officer, Tirupur.

For Appellant : Mr.M.Murali Vinodh
 For R1 : Mr.Ma.P.Thangavel
 Judgment
This appeal has been filed by the appellant/Transport Corporation challenging the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P. No.306 of 2012 dated 12.09.2022.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

2.The claim petition was filed stating that on 16.02.2012 at 6.00 p.m., when the 1st respondent/claimant was riding two wheeler bearing Registration No. TN 39 S 6716, the bus bearing registration No. TN 38 N 0775 came in a rash and negligent manner and rammed against the 1st respondent's/claimant's vehicle; as a result of which he had suffered injuries on the right hand, right hip, fingers, lost his teeth and abrasion all over his body as that he was entitled to a compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
3.The
1st respondent/driver of the bus remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

The The Managing Director vs Kuppusamy on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98241595/
1

appellant/Transport Corporation filed a counter denying all the averments made in the claim petition and stated that the claimant was on the influence of alcohol and he was carrying liquor bottles with him and that in any case, the claim was excessive.
4.The 2nd respondent/claimant examined two witnesses on his side and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3.

On behalf of the appellant/Transport Corporation, R.W.1/driver was examined and marked Ex.R1.
5.The

Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence held that the 1st respondent/driver was guilty of negligence and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the appellant/Transport Corporation is liable to pay compensation amount of Rs. 4,46,844/-
6.Aggrieved by the said order, the appellant/Transport Corporation had preferred the instant appeal challenging the findings with regard to negligence.
7.

The Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Transport Corporation would submit that admittedly, the 2nd respondent/claimant was carrying liquor bottles in his two wheeler, which would show that he contributed to the accident and that the finding of the Tribunal fixing the entire liability on the appellant/Transport Corporation is erroneous and hence the Tribunal ought to have fixed contributory negligence on the 2nd respondent/claimant.
The Learned counsel could not point out any error in the computation with regard to quantum of compensation.

8.The Learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent/claimant per contra, would submit that the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 would clearly show that the accident took place only due to the rash a n d n e g l i g e n t d r i v i n g o f t h e 1 s t r e s p o n d e n t . T h e o n l y g r o u n d o n w h i c h t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
appellant
/ Transport
Corporation claims contributory negligence is the 2nd respondent/claimant was carrying liquor bottles with him.
He would further submit that in the absence of any evidence to show that there was contributory negligence on the part of the 2nd respondent/claimant, contributory negligence cannot be fixed.

9.This Court on perusal of the award of the Tribunal, and on hearing the counsel for either parties finds that the only question in the instant appeal is whether the claimant had contributed to the accident.
It is seen that the there is no evidence to suggest that the 1 st respondent/claimant was under the influence of alcohol.

In the absence of such evidence, this court is of the view that merely because the 1st respondent/claimant had carried liquor bottles in his two wheeler, it cannot be said that he had contributed to the accident.
The finding of the Tribunal that the 1st respondent/claimant is not guilty of contributory negligence
is factually and legally correct.
Hence, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the award passed by the Tribunal.

10.In view of the above, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is confirmed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis together with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The appellant/Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the entire compensation awarded by the Tribunal along with interest and costs,
less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of a receipt of copy of this Judgment.

On such deposit the 1st respondent/claimant is permitted to withdraw the The Managing Director vs Kuppusamy on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98241595/
2 entire award amount along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
